pairs.subject: production-trace-scoring
pairs.evidence: crates/runner/src/score_traces.rs:322 Trace sampling admits a trace when its hash leaves a remainder of zero mod N. Changing N therefore draws a new admitted set instead of only adding traces, and nothing in the posted score body (lines 172-178) records the rate or the stratum that admitted the trace, so verdicts cannot be reweighted correctly after N changes.

techniques.evidence: crates/runner/src/score_traces.rs:322 The FNV-1a hash is stable and keyed on trace id, and the pure predicate is applied twice (lines 238 and 128), which is all correct. But this is the fixed-residue mod-N form that the technique names as the failure: the samples do not nest when N changes. The rate in force is also not stamped on the verdict.

crates/runner/src/score_traces.rs:318 The override is an explicit --errors-always flag. It keys on the trace's own status (ts.status == "error") and sits below the already-scored short-circuit (line 315) and above the hash bucket, which is the order the technique requires. Caveats: there is no stated ceiling for surges, and the verdict does not record which stratum admitted the trace.

crates/runner/src/score_traces.rs:113 A quiet window (--settle-secs, default 120s) is computed on every cycle and applied through until= on the trace's ended time. It is stateless, which is correct. But no maximum-age ceiling exists, so a trace that keeps emitting never falls before the cutoff and is never judged. The technique explicitly requires that ceiling.

crates/runner/src/score_traces.rs:16 The runner does not compose the receipt itself. It posts to /v1/traces/:id/score and the server stamps the coverage. I checked crates/api/src/traces.rs:263 (`coverage: whole_trace.then(|| trace.coverage())`) and the FNV digest over the root exchange in crates/core/src/trace.rs:157-161.

crates/runner/src/score_traces.rs:289 Only `changed` drift reopens a trace for scoring. `grown` drift and verdicts without a receipt still count as covered. A corrected trace (stale verdict plus a fresh one) stays closed. Re-scores still pass through should_score, so they keep the sample gate. Tests at lines 409-438 pin all of this.

crates/runner/src/score.rs:83 The per-event queue is served by the server, but it is not scoped per rubric: Store::list_unscored_events (crates/store/src/lib.rs:1275) takes only project, prompt and limit. An event scored under any rubric therefore never enters the queue for a second rubric. The trace path has no server-side unscored queue at all. The client pages the newest `limit` settled traces and checks each trace's detail for scores, so traces already scored keep using up the window.

pairs.registryProposal: The rust--unscored-work-queue application says 'already scored' is checked against the rubric label throughout. That is true only for the whole-trace path (score_traces.rs). The per-event `?unscored=1` queue it uses as its main example is not rubric-scoped, so the application overstates conformance on the 'scope the queue per rubric' rule.
